## Closing {#sec-close}

::: {.skeleton}
*Final heading to come.*

- Where we stand: classical $d - 1$, quantum $d^2 - 1$, both reached.
  Same proof, quadratically larger space
- Close the memory reading: a qubit memory survives at most three
  uses, in general $d^2 - 1$; after that it forgets exactly
- Maximal roots need not sit close to $P$
  (Proposition 3.5[^prop35]). Example: the qubit root with factors
  $\tfrac12$
- Optional, personal: the history in the thesis. Complete positivity
  held up the general construction for a long time; the Clifford
  channels came first
- Outlook on part 2: a rigid family with few parameters. How much of
  $d^2 - 1$ survives? Almost all of it, up to a factor of two
- The thesis as the source[^thesis]
:::

[^prop35]: A. Ahlbrecht, F. Richter and R. F. Werner, "How long can
it take for a quantum channel to forget everything?",
arXiv:1205.0693 (2012), Proposition 3.5.

[^thesis]: F. Richter, *Finite Roots of Completely Depolarizing
Channels*, Diploma thesis, Institute for Theoretical Physics,
Leibniz Universität Hannover, September 2010.
[PDF in this site's repository](https://github.com/Florian2Richter/florian2richter.github.io/blob/main/reference/Diplomarbeit_Florian.pdf).
